Subject: Realtime chat stalling — intermittent 1–8s gaps in token arrival

Diego,

We started seeing intermittent stalls in our live chat feature this morning (around 08:50–09:10 PDT). In many sessions the server returns partial chunks and then there is a 1–8s gap before the next chunk arrives; other sessions look fine. This is causing our UI to appear stuck and triggers our client-side fallback which degrades UX.

Attached is a short pcap and server-side stream logs for two affected session IDs: SESS-ccf8 and SESS-ef12. We're on the Redwood hosted inference endpoint (us-west) using the standard streaming API and haven't changed our client code.

Can you confirm if this is a known issue and whether there are recommended mitigations on our side while you investigate? We have an upcoming demo at 11:00 and need a short-term workaround.

Thanks,
Brian
Product Ops — HomeBank

Subject: Re: Realtime chat stalling — intermittent 1–8s gaps in token arrival

Brian — thanks for the detailed repro and the logs. We're looking at this as a priority. Short answers up front: this is a streaming token pacing anomaly we're actively triaging, and we have three short-term mitigations you can apply immediately on the client to reduce user-visible stalls while we investigate server-side fixes.

Immediate customer-side mitigations (apply now):
- Enable a client-side chunk-timeout of 500–800ms. If no new chunk arrives in that window, show a subtle "typing" indicator and keep the connection open (do not fail the stream).
- Switch to a short polling fallback (non-streaming) for demo sessions: set streaming_timeout_ms = 2000 and fallback to single-response mode only for sessions older than your demo TTL.
- Reduce max_tokens_per_request to lower average generation length (this shortens each chunk run and improves pacing).

We suspect the issue is related to intermittent scheduling delays at the us-west edge when prefix KV cache misses coincide with longer OOM-protected kernel swaps — this can cause bursts of 50–400ms at the runtime, and multiple bursts look like 1–8s stalls at the client.

Action items for you: please attach a full trace for SESS-ccf8 if possible (we have the partial logs but need the long trace). Also, enable the lightweight SDK setting `enable_heuristic_chunking=true` if you can; it will smooth chunk windowing for the next 24–48 hours.

I'll loop Laura and Rishi for the server-side triage and we'll send a prioritized mitigation plan and ETA in the next 2–3 hours.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Customer Reliability Lead — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Realtime chat stalling — triage notes and temporary server-side controls

Quick triage notes based on Brian's logs and our early telemetry: 
- Symptom: bursty inter-chunk gaps concentrated on a small subset of edge instances in us-west-2; not correlated with client-side packet loss.
- Likely proximate cause: increased tail latency when KV-prefix cache miss hits coincide with a longer GPU kernel swap on models using large KV caches. In short: a small set of requests fall onto a cold path.

Short-term server-side mitigations we can apply (hours):
1) Temporarily increase per-edge request concurrency cap (soft cap) to avoid queuing that amplifies tail bursts. Rollout time: ~2 hours to stage, 3–4 hours to full edge rollout.
2) Enable "kv-prefix-hot-cache" for the affected model family on the impacted shard group — will reduce cold path misses. Rollout: ~4–6 hours, requires canary verification.
3) Push a routing tweak to bias new sessions away from the two noisy hosts (immediate, minutes) — low risk.

Longer-term: we should instrument per-session sample pacing and add a heuristic to smooth bursts at the runtime level (tracked as INF-7219). That will be a targeted engineering task (2–3 sprints).

I'll coordinate the rollout with infra and watch the canary. Diego — please include the customer-facing mitigations you proposed and offer a short credit for the demo interruption if we determine customer impact > 5 minutes.

Laura Bennett
Senior SRE, Inference — Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident: token pacing spike — findings, actions taken, and recommended client settings

Brian / Kris — quick post-incident summary and next steps. Thank you for the logs and for applying the client-side fallbacks; that helped keep your demo running.

What happened (summary):
- Between 08:45–10:30 PDT on 2027-06-01 we observed intermittent token-pacing spikes on a subset of us-west edge hosts servicing the streaming API. The client symptom was 1–8s pauses between stream chunks.
- Root cause (short): cache-miss amplified runtime scheduling on a small number of hosts; a combination of KV prefix misses and concurrent swap activity produced tail bursts. Tracking INF-7219 for the deeper runtime change.

Actions we took:
- Immediately: recommended client mitigations (chunk-timeout, short polling fallback, heuristics) — you confirmed applying `enable_heuristic_chunking=true` during the demo.
- Within 6 hours: we pushed a routing bias away from two noisy hosts and enabled a hot-prefix cache for the affected model family in the us-west shard group. Canary verified; rollout completed at ~14:30 PDT on 2027-06-01.
- Monitoring: added a short-term alert (edge.pacing.tail-50ms) plus a dashboard to surface per-shard pacing anomalies.

Recommended durable client settings (please adopt permanently):
- chunk_timeout_ms: 600
- enable_heuristic_chunking: true
- fallback_mode_threshold_ms: 1800 (switch to non-streaming only when cumulative gap > threshold)
- max_tokens_per_request: reduce by ~20% for high-concurrency sessions

Next steps from Redwood:
- INF-7219 (runtime pacing heuristics) is prioritized and assigned to the inference runtime squad; ETA for initial release: Q3 2027.
- We'll offer a goodwill credit for the impacted demo window; I'll follow up with your account team (Deal ID: HB-2027-Q2-Expansion).
- Optional: we can schedule a 30-minute technical review this week to walk through the logs and the rollout details — propose Thu 2027-06-03 09:00 PDT, let me know if that works.

Again — apologies for the disruption and thanks for the quick coordination. Please ping me directly if you see any reoccurrence.

Best regards,
Diego Fernandez
Customer Reliability Lead — Redwood Inference
